title: Lift Aloud the Voice of Praise
description: Lift Aloud the Voice of Praise in Tonic Solfa to PLEYEL'S HYMN, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Ephraim Peabody wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 713 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Ordination or Installation”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to PLEYEL'S HYMN; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lift a-loud the voice of praise! God, our Fa-ther and our Friend, Hear the prayer and song we raise, Weak, yet trust-ing, we would bend.

lines: Lift aloud the voice of praise!
God, our Father and our Friend,
Hear the prayer and song we raise,
Weak, yet trusting, we would bend.
May he teach as Christ hath taught,
Tread the path his Saviour trod.
To the vineyard may he come
Skilled to draw thy children home,
Taught to give the darkened light.
Bind us heart to heart in love;
Flock and pastor, we would tend

licence: Public domain: Ephraim Peabody died in 1856.
credits: Words by Ephraim Peabody (1807–1856), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to PLEYEL'S HYMN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
